_comment: R-124 WRITER principal: create only, under one prefix.
TWO statements, because AWS requires s3:PutObjectRetention whenever an
upload supplies Object Lock settings. With s3:PutObject alone this
principal could not have written a single journal object -- every append
would have been denied. Found by live provisioning, not by any test here.
THE COST, STATED: that permission lets the writer EXTEND a COMPLIANCE lock.
It cannot shorten one and cannot delete or rewrite the protected version --
S3 forbids that to every principal, including the account root. So the
claim 'the writer can never change retention' is too strong; the durable
promise is that it cannot shorten protection or destroy a locked version.
The retention statement is itself fenced to COMPLIANCE and >= 28 days.
The writer has NO read, list or delete permission. Its application mirror
